summary.text: A 74-year-old woman of Arab ethnicity with dermatomyositis diagnosed in 2011 (hypomyopathic, anti-Mi-2 detected, Pneumocystis pneumonia four months later) maintained remission on prednisone and azathioprine until the disease recurred in September 2019. She presented on October 1, 2019 with a two-week history of severe fatigue, rash and dry cough, with fine bibasal crepitations, oxygen saturation of 96% in room air and ground-glass opacities on HRCT.

Anti-Jo-1 antibodies (51 and 50.5 U) were found with negative MDA5 and other myositis antibodies, and anti-synthetase syndrome was diagnosed. She was prescribed prednisone 80 mg/day, azathioprine and tacrolimus; the cutaneous eruptions completely resolved within three weeks, but the respiratory function deteriorated with 82% room-air saturation, and she was admitted from October 21 to November 27, 2019 with expanding ground-glass opacities, FDG SUVmax 4.2, FVC 59% and ferritin rising to 1,695 μg/L; lavage excluded infection.

Methylprednisolone pulses and IVIG gave only a temporary ferritin fall to 1,192 μg/L before it rebounded to 1973 μg/L, so tofacitinib 5 mg twice daily with methylprednisolone 60 mg/day was started (dated October 30, 2019 in the text and November 1 in the table caption) and azathioprine and tacrolimus stopped. Ferritin fell to 915 μg/L and PET SUVmax to 1.9 by November 18, 2019 when nintedanib 150 mg twice daily was added, and prednisolone was tapered.

FVC fell to 37% of predicted by December 1 and recovered to 50% by March 9, 2020, when oxygen saturation was 97% in room air and ferritin 304 μg/L. CT on day 43 showed reduced ground-glass opacities with more prominent septal thickening. Cytomegalovirus reactivation was treated with valganciclovir, mild macrocytic anemia and ALT doubling occurred, and the NK cell deficiency and other hematologic abnormalities resolved except the CD4/CD8 ratio.

Chest CT and ^(18)F-FDG PET/CT scans in anti-Jo-1 antibody-positive RPILD. Serial axial CT scans of upper and middle (A) as well as lower lobes of the lung (B) showed patchy ground–glass opacities (red arrows) on presentation (October 1, 2019) and worsening on hospital admission (October 22, 2019). Interlobular septal thickening (green arrows) was observed ∼6 weeks after starting therapy with tofacitinib (December 11, 2019). caption_evidence.quote:
FIGURE 2
Timeline of pharmacologic interventions, changes in serum ferritin levels and FVC from October 2019 until March 2020. While the patient was treated with high-dose prednisone, azathioprine and tacrolimus ①, the respiratory function suddenly deteriorated and serum ferritin levels (y-axis left) rose from 428 to 1,695 μg/L (reference range 13–150 μg/L, dashed line). Pulse therapy with methylprednisolone and IVIG ② were followed by an ephemeral decrease in serum ferritin levels, which rebounded to the maximum measured value of 1973 μg/L. With the administration of tofacitinib first ③ and nintedanib three weeks later ④ we witnessed an immediate clinical improvement and a prompt, continuous decrease in serum ferritin levels to 304 μg/L, which allowed to taper prednisone in short, 10-days intervals. An initial decline of FVC from 59% to 37% was followed by a modest recovery to 50% of predicted value (y-axis right; dotted line). Details of doses of the medications used, including the tapering scheme of the corticosteroid, are found in the main text.

caption_evidence.quote:
FIGURE 3
In (A), changes in counts of CD3^(−)CD56^(+)CD16^(+) NK cells and CD4^(+) T cells are plotted over time. Serial measurements of circulating NK cells/μl (y-axis left; dashed line) and CD4^(+) T cells/µl (y-axis right; dotted line) by flow cytometry disclosed a persistent, severe numerical NK cell deficiency (mean 18.5 ± 11.5 cells/µl, reference range 100–645 cells/µl), whereas CD4^(+) T cells initially fell to 264 cells/µl on the second day of admission (October 23) and fluctuated considerably within reference range thereafter (mean 1,389 ± 650 cells/µl, reference range 322–1750 cells/µl). NK cell counts returned to normal levels (106 cells/µl) at the end of the observation period. In (B), a representative example of flow cytometry histograms using standard gating strategy is shown. CD45^(+)/SSC gate was applied to identify peripheral blood lymphocytes, followed by CD19^(+)/SSC, CD3^(+)/SSC, CD8^(+) vs. CD4^(+) subsets and finally CD19^(+) vs. NK cells identified as CD3^(−)CD19^(−)CD56^(+) CD16^(+) lymphocytes, which were nearly absent (histogram #5).
